title: 4/17/2026 | MISSION POWER | PC | BRIEF COMMENTS IN SUPPORT OF CHAIRMAN GLEESON'S "GRADUAL ESCALATOR FRAMEWORK" FOR GRADUAL POSTING OF THE $50,000 IA SECURITY POSTING

=== March 12th meeting draft - gradual escalator.pdf ===
                                            PUCT Project No. 58481

 RULEMAKMING TO IMPLEMENT                           §         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                         §                     TEXAS
 STANDARS UNDER PURA §37.0561                       §


 BRIEF COMMENTS OF MISSION POWER REGARDING CHAIRMAN GLEESON’S PROPOSED
          “GRADUAL ESCALATOR” FOR THE $50,000 IA SECURITY POSTING

1. INTRODUCTION

Mission Power seeks to respectfully highlight to participants the Commissioners’ March 12th endorsement of a
“gradual escalator as a framework” with regard to the $50,000 Intermediate Agreement posting.

                                      March 12th Open Meeting Minute 59:

“I think its appropriate to take all these gating issues that we’ve been talking about and try to find ways that we
  can align the regulatory commitments we’re looking for with the commercial milestones in the development
 process for these large loads. And so that’s how I’m starting to think about this, and think about it through
 the lens of a kind of gradual escalator so if it’s $50,000 of financial commitment perhaps initially you owe,
let’s just say for argument’s sake $10,000 or $20,000 and then that escalates up as you progress through the
        kind of commercial viability of the commercial operations of the facility.” – Chairman Gleeson

                     The Chairman goes on to request that this change be made in the PFP.

         (meeting link for reference: https://www.adminmonitor.com/tx/puct/open_meeting/20260312/)

In reviewing the comments submitted through April 16th under this docket 58481 since the March 12th, 2026 PFP
publication, we could not find many (or perhaps any) references to the Chairman’s “gradual escalator” concept,
despite the numerous concerns voiced about the potential onerous impacts of the $50,000 requirement as printed
in the PFP. This led us to believe that many are unaware of the Chairman’s proposal.

2. HIGHLIGHTING CHAIRMAN GLEESON’S “GRADUAL ESCALATOR” PROPOSAL.

We wish to highlight for the participant community that in the open meeting it was determined that Chairman
Gleeson’s “gradual escalator” concept was of a nature that could not be included in the PFP at the time of
publishing, and thus it amounts to a powerful concept that Commissioners endorsed but was nonetheless
not put in the PFP due to the aforementioned determination, and thus apparently is not well known. One
would probably have had to have been in attendance or watched the video of it to know of its popularity among
the Commissioners in that open meeting discussion.

3. “GRADUAL ESCALATOR” CONCEPT LEFT OUT OF PFP DESPITE ENDORSEMENT.

                                   March 12th Open Meeting Minute 1.06.49

“Staff is absolutely open to hearing about and we welcome your feedback but we specifically want stakeholders
to provide commentary on the appropriate way to handle system upgrades, the appropriate treatment of the 80/20
proportion, and other things you talked about but those will be addressed through the comments and as revisions
to the rule as we get to the proposal for adoption stage. Most notably we will not be changing anything in the
PFP related to aligning the delivery of those financial securities to the regular business cycle that you were
talking about so we’re not going to be introducing the concept of a graduated fee over the course of this process
in the Proposal for Publication.”
 4. CONCLUSION

Because a “gradual escalator framework” for the $50,000 AI deposit: (1) has the support of Commissioners, (2)
is critical to regulatory and business alignment for all the reasons Chairman Gleeson stated, (3) can solve many
of the issues that parties appear to be concerned about, and (4) does not appear in the text of the PFP despite the
broad and reasoned support of Commissioners, we feel it is in the best interest of the community that we draw
attention to the Chairman’s comments at minute 59 of the March 12th open meeting vide
(https://www.adminmonitor.com/tx/puct/open_meeting/20260312/).

We believe it is a powerful concept and we will be supporting the Chairman’s “gradual escalator framework.”

Respectfully Submitted,




Javier Vega
Manager, Mission Power
